summary: Raerby's brokers: the banks mediation, arbiters and the moot, envoys, the broker fleet and peace at sea.

broker_captains.name: Brokers Between the Islands
broker_captains.desc: When two isles quarrel over a bank, a wreck or a debt, they send for a Raerby captain. His word is not law, but both sides have agreed in advance to hear it.

compass_of_raer.name: Raer's Compass
compass_of_raer.desc: The compass of old Captain Raer hangs in the council hall, its needle bent but faithful. The isles say that Raerby always knows which way is north, even when it pretends not to.

arbiters.name: Arbiters at Sea
arbiters.desc: Raerby's arbiters ride on the largest ship of each sailing and sit in judgment on the deck. A dispute between two crews is settled before either reaches port.

peace_of_the_pupor_spirit.name: The Peace of the Pupor
peace_of_the_pupor_spirit.desc: For a season the captains of the Pupor agree that no ship shall be seized without a hearing. The corsairs grumble, and the merchants sleep a little better.

brokers_of_charters_spirit.name: Brokers of Charters
brokers_of_charters_spirit.desc: Raerby's captains carry other realms' charters to the Charter's table and bring back the replies. They are paid in goodwill and, now and then, in coin.

long_patrol.name: The Long Patrol
long_patrol.desc: A line of fast galleys keeps watch from the eastern reefs to the western banks, each hailing the next at dusk. No corsair can slip through without being seen.

brokers_of_peace_spirit.name: Brokers of Peace
brokers_of_peace_spirit.desc: Raerby stands between the fleets with an olive branch and no weapons. Its captains are heard on both sides, and its young men are asked why they do not fight.

raerby_vote.title: The Captains Vote
raerby_vote.desc: The council of captains meets on the deck of the oldest ship in harbour, as the custom is. The old captains want to keep the broker's trade as it is, and the young ones want a bigger fleet and a sharper edge.

isles_envoy.title: Envoys from the Isles
isles_envoy.desc: A Raerby captain stands in the hall of Parim with a letter from the isles of the Pupor. He asks nothing for his own crown and wishes only that the king know the isles keep the sea-lanes quiet, and that they would be friends.

focuses.name: The Captains' Council
focuses.desc: Raerby is governed by a council of captains who elect a Captain-Speaker. Lemo Raer holds the wheel now, and the council meets whenever a ship is sighted in the offing.

focuses.name: The Speaker's Wheel
focuses.desc: The Captain-Speaker's chair is a ship's wheel set on a plinth. He keeps one hand on it when he speaks, so that all remember he is a sailor first.

focuses.name: The Old Captains
focuses.desc: The greybeards of Raerby have sailed every sea of the isles, and their word counts in the council. A seat is kept for each, with a cushion and a pipe.

focuses.name: Raer's Compass
focuses.desc: Founder Raer's bent compass is carried in procession and set in a niche in the council hall. The isles say it always points at the nearest quarrel.

focuses.name: The Council Elects
focuses.desc: Once in four years the captains vote on who holds the wheel. The election is held at sea, so that no captain can say he was not on board.

focuses.name: Brokers of the Isles
focuses.desc: Raerby's trade is small, but its standing is large. The council writes it into its law: a captain who is asked to judge must judge, and judge fairly.

focuses.name: Arbiters at Sea
focuses.desc: Osk Faran is the most respected arbiter in the isles, and the council gives him a ship of his own. Wherever he sails, quarrels grow quieter.

focuses.name: The Banks Dispute
focuses.desc: Nondondor and the Seite Isles fish the same southern banks, and both say the banks are theirs. Raerby offers to judge, and sends a captain with the offer in both hands.

focuses.name: A Registry of Fishing Rights
focuses.desc: Every pier, every bank and every net-right is written in a single book kept at Raerby. A fisher who has quarrelled with his neighbour may open it at the right page.

focuses.name: The Moot of Captains
focuses.desc: Captains of every isle gather at Raerby for a moot on the mid-summer tide. They talk, drink and swear a few small oaths, and leave a little less likely to quarrel.

focuses.name: The Peace of the Pupor
focuses.desc: The moot makes a pledge: no ship shall be taken without a hearing, no captain hanged without a witness. The corsairs are not pleased, but they are listening.

focuses.name: Envoys to the Mainland
focuses.desc: When the isles must speak to a court on the mainland, a Raerby captain usually carries the letter. The council makes it formal, with seals and robes.

focuses.name: The Western Courts
focuses.desc: Raerby's captains stop at every harbour of the western shore and carry the courts' letters to one another. They hear much, and say little of it.

effects.tooltip: Raerby's captains carry letters for every court of the western shore.

focuses.name: A Word for Parim
focuses.desc: A captain with a good coat and a better tongue is sent to Parim. He is to say that the isles want the lanes quiet and have no quarrel with the king.

focuses.name: Brokers of Charters
focuses.desc: Raerby carries the Pupor Charter to every chart house and brings back their seals. If the Charter has been founded, it takes its own place at the table.

focuses.name: The Brokers' Seal
focuses.desc: The council cuts a new seal for its brokers: a compass over two clasped hands. A letter that bears it is read, in every harbour of the isles, without suspicion.

focuses.name: The Raerby Yards
focuses.desc: The slips at Raerby have been quiet for a generation. The council hires shipwrights from Adel and lays down new keels, long and lean.

focuses.name: Fast Hulls
focuses.desc: The yard-master drafts a galley with a narrow beam and forty oars. She is meant to be fast enough to catch a corsair skiff and strong enough to hold it.

focuses.name: The Broker Fleet
focuses.desc: Ilka Raer takes command of the new galleys, and teaches her crews to board as quickly as they row. She is the Captain-Speaker's daughter and the best sailor of her house.

focuses.name: The Long Patrol
focuses.desc: The galleys sail in a long line from the eastern reefs to the western banks, each ship in sight of the next. They keep the line through gale and fog.

focuses.name: Corsair Hunters
focuses.desc: Fast galleys are sent after the worst of the corsair captains. They are told to bring them back alive when they can, and to bring back their ships in any case.

focuses.name: The Harbour of Raerby
focuses.desc: The harbour is dredged and a second mole is built to hold the sea. A ship that anchors in Raerby sleeps easy even in a gale.

focuses.name: Rope and Sail
focuses.desc: Sailmakers and ropewalkers set up their sheds along the shore. Raerby buys less and sells more, and its captains stop paying strangers for canvas.

focuses.name: The Exchange
focuses.desc: A small exchange hall opens on the quay, where factors trade bills drawn on every island. It is a brokers' kind of business, and Raerby is good at it.

focuses.name: Raerby's Stores
focuses.desc: Barns on the hill hold grain, salt-meat and dried fruit against a bad season. The Captain-Speaker holds the keys and has promised to share them with any neighbour in need.

focuses.name: Every Sail Welcome
focuses.desc: Raerby has never turned a ship away at the harbour mouth. The council puts the custom into writing, and nails it to the pier.

focuses.name: A Southern Ship
focuses.desc: A fast ship has been seen running north, with elves among her crew. The Captain-Speaker orders the harbour lamps lit, whatever her business.

focuses.name: The War at Sea
focuses.desc: The fleets of the great realms are moving. The council meets in the night, for a broker has no place in a war, and Raerby must find one.

focuses.name: Brokers of Peace
focuses.desc: Raerby offers its ships and its arbiters as go-betweens. Its captains carry truce flags between fleets, and ask for nothing but safe passage.

focuses.name: Ships for the Crossing
focuses.desc: The western host needs hulls, and Raerby has them. The council sells a few of its galleys at a fair price and hopes they are not used to cross the sea twice.

focuses.name: Envoys to the Heir
focuses.desc: The stranger from the south has been named and has returned. A Raerby captain is sent to ask what he needs from the isles, and to offer him the ear of every harbour.

focuses.name: The Banks-Court Remembered
focuses.desc: Raerby's mediation of the banks began as the league's own banks-court, and the brokers have the rolls to prove it. If the Charter means to swear the old league again, Raerby expects its old seat at the table.
